name: Starting the process
description: Two quick checks to get the drainage system running -- the actual job Section Nine was sent to do. Unlike this session's other checks, these aren't zero-stakes flavour: this is the real assignment, and failure has a real, small cost. Success or failure, finishing both checks is what provokes the fight.

checks.name: Get power back to the drainage line

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Power's back cleanly, first try. Whoever did it gets a nod from the others -- small, but noticed.
outcomes.failure: It comes online anyway, roughly -- a jolt through the panel, a bang from somewhere below. Loud enough that nothing about the next part is a surprise to anything down there.
outcomes.criticalFailure: Same as failure, plus a shower of sparks that's more alarming than dangerous -- nobody's hurt, but everyone's attention is on the panel instead of the room for a moment.

checks.name: Clear the physical jam in the compactor feed

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Clean and fast -- the mechanism starts up smooth.
outcomes.failure: It clears, but takes a shove, and the system lurches into motion rougher than it should -- if the compactor-cycle subsystem is in play, Encroachment starts at 1 instead of 0.
outcomes.criticalFailure: Same as failure, and whoever's closest gets a face full of stagnant water for their trouble. Cosmetic only -- no damage, just a very bad start to the night.

notes: Both checks should be attempted before the fight starts -- assign them to whichever two players want them, or split one each if more than two want in. The instant both resolve (regardless of success/failure), the fight and the optional compactor-cycle both begin. This is the one place in Session One's checks where failure has a small real cost rather than being free -- flagged deliberately, since it's the actual job, not an optional flourish.
